Description: Report a property suspected of being used in violation of City zoning bylaws, such as illegal commercial use in a residential zone.
Tip: Provide as much detail as possible about the suspected violation to support the investigation.

Description: Report a container placed out for collection at the wrong location, on the wrong day, or outside the scheduled window.
Tip:
The complainant's name and phone number are required, location where the garbage can be found and the type of complaint, e.g., waste put out on the wrong day, dumping, etc.

The officer may contact the complainant if additional information is needed.

Description: Report a suspected watermain break, such as water bubbling up through pavement, large puddles forming in dry conditions, or a noticeable loss of water pressure.
Tip: If water is flooding a road or property, call 311 directly rather than filing online to expedite the response.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~2 hours
Repair / Action: ~16 hours depending on severity
Restoration / Completion: up to 24 months (in case of watermain repair)

Description: Report an emergency water service line burst or a line that needs to be immediately shut off due to a plumbing failure.
Tip: If water is flooding your property, turn off your interior shutoff valve immediately and call 311 directly.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~2 hours
Repair / Action: depends on ownership (City vs private)

Description: Report a complete loss of water service at your property when there is no known planned shutoff or watermain work in your area.
Tip: Check if neighbours are also affected as a watermain issue may already be under investigation.

Description: Report a leak on the water service line connecting the City watermain to your property.
Tip: Turn off your interior water shutoff valve if the leak is significant to minimize damage while you wait.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~4 hours
Repair / Action: 5 business days (standard) or ~24 hours (emergency)
Restoration / Completion: up to 24 months (in case of service line repair)

service_request_type: Water Service Line-Check Water Service Box
Description: Request for Toronto Water to check or repair a water service box on the sidewalk or front lawn. Note: A water service box is a round brown valve on the sidewalk or front lawn. Service boxes give the City access to shut off water to your home
Tip: This is a maintenance check. If you have no water or a suspected leak, use the appropriate service request instead.

service_request_type: Waste Or Illegal Dumping On Private Property
Description: Report a concern about the accumulation of waste, litter, standing water or witnessed illegal dumping on private property (e.g. derelict vehicles, accumulation of refuse, stagnant water in unused pools).
Tip: Provide the property address and describe the waste type to help bylaw officers assess the violation.
Timeline:
Initial Response: within ~10 days (investigation initiation)
Repair / Action: enforcement and cleanup order

Description: Report a damaged, cracked, heaved, or uneven sidewalk, walkway, or sidewalk bay that poses a tripping hazard. City inspectors monitor sidewalk conditions during road inspections and track sections in need of repair — priority is given to the bays in greatest need.
Tip: Report minor damage online; for serious hazards such as a large raised slab, note whether it is a tripping risk so staff can prioritize it accordingly.

Description: Report noise or sound-induced vibration that is unreasonable and persistent — such as continuous building alarms, equipment noise, or neighbours dropping heavy objects at unreasonable hours. This covers any noise heard or felt for 10 minutes or more, or intermittently heard or felt for a total of 10 minutes within one hour. Typical household sounds are exempt
Tip: Keep a log of dates, times, and duration of each noise occurrence — bylaw officers may ask for this record to support an investigation or court proceeding.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~24 hours (priority-based)
Repair / Action: investigation and enforcement

Description: Report a City-owned tree that has been illegally cut, removed, or damaged without a permit. Examples include cutting down a protected tree or dumping construction fill in a Ravine Protection Area without a permit.
Tip: Provide Incident address, estimated number of trees involved, location, date, time, vehicle plate number and name. Contact  311 within 6 months of violation
Timeline:
Initial Response: 72 hours to 21 days depending on priority
Repair / Action: investigation and enforcement
Restoration / Completion: up to 12 months

Description: Request the planting of a new City street tree at or near your property as part of the urban forest program.
Tip: Based on timing of request and type of tree, requests can be completed within 12 months
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~8 weeks (assessment)
Repair / Action: planting scheduled within 12–18 months

Description: Report a fallen or dangerously hanging tree or large branch on City property that poses an immediate safety risk.
Tip: If a tree has fallen on a vehicle, power line, or structure, call 911 first before filing this request.
Timeline:
Initial Response:  ~72 hours depending on severity
Restoration / Completion: may take months

Description: Report a malfunctioning, dark, or damaged traffic signal at an intersection. Use this for flashing lights, blank signals, or signals showing incorrect sequences.
Tip: If the signal is completely dark, treat the intersection as a four-way stop until it is repaired.

service_request_type: Timeliness Of Service Complaint Road Operations
Description: File a complaint if a Road Operations service request was not completed within the promised timeframe.
Tip: Include your original service request number so staff can review the case history.

Description: Report a maintenance concern, damage, or graffiti on street furniture (transit shelters, benches, litter bins, info pillars, posting structures, automated toilets, bicycle locking rings, etc.), or request the installation, relocation, or removal of a street furniture element on the public right-of-way.
Tip: For installation or relocation requests, emailing the Street Furniture unit directly may result in a faster response than filing through 311.

Description: Report a stray animal that is confined or trapped in a yard, vehicle, or structure and cannot get out on its own.
Tip: Provide the exact address and describe where the animal is confined to help officers respond quickly.
Timeline: Initial Response: within ~5 hours subject to call volume

Description: Report a stray dog or cat roaming loose without an owner in a public area.
Tip: Note the animal's breed, colour, and last known location to help officers locate it quickly.
Timeline: Initial Response: within ~5 hours subject to call volume

Description: Submit an application or inquiry related to City signage permits, including business signs, banners, or other sign installations.
Tip: Ensure your sign meets zoning and size bylaws before applying to avoid delays.
Timeline:
Repair / Action: review within ~3 months
Restoration / Completion: permit issued within ~3–10 days after approval

Description: Report a City-maintained sidewalk that has not been cleared of snow and is hazardous to pedestrians.
Tip: Property owners are responsible for their adjacent sidewalk within 12 hours of snowfall. This service only covers City-maintained sidewalks. Snow accumulation to be more than 2cm.
Timeline: Initial Response: within ~12–72 hours depending on snowfall and priority routes

Description: A sidewalk cleaning service request is a request to remove larger items such as construction debris or items left due to a traffic accident, not litter.
Tip: Sidewalk cleaning is scheduled seasonally.
Timeline:
Initial Response: varies based on seasonal schedule
Repair / Action: scheduled in next cleaning cycle

Description: Report a blocked or backed-up sewer service line at your property. Use this if you have sewage backup in your basement or drains are not clearing.
Tip: Do not use any drains or toilets until the blockage is cleared to prevent further backup.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~4 hours
Repair / Action: ~24 hours (may extend during high demand)
Restoration / Completion: up to 24 months (in case of service line repair)

Description: Road sinking (also referred to as road settlement) occurs when the roadway surface drops, settles, or becomes uneven even though the asphalt surface may remain mostly intact. Visible signs may include ponding of water or depressions on the road surface.
Tip: If the sinking is severe or worsening rapidly, also call 311 directly to flag it as urgent.

Description: Request salt application on an icy or slippery City road to improve traction and safety for drivers.
Tip: Main roads and transit routes are salted first. Local residential streets may take longer.Multiple rounds might be needed (values provided for one round).
Timeline: Initial Response: 2–8 hours depending on road priority

Description: Report a pothole or surface damage on a City road that poses a hazard to vehicles or cyclists. Use this for any road defect that needs repair.
Tip: Note the nearest intersection or landmark so the crew can locate the pothole quickly.
Timeline:
Initial Response: 24 Hours (in case of Emergency)
Repair / Action: 4–21 days depending on road classification

Description: Request snow plowing on a City road that has not been cleared after a snowfall. Use this if your road remains impassable after the standard clearing window.
Tip: Main roads and transit routes are plowed first. Local residential streets may take longer.Multiple rounds might be needed (values provided for one round).
Timeline: Initial Response: 2–14 hours depending on road classification

Description: Report that your blue recycling bin has gone missing or been stolen from your property.
Tip: Check nearby properties first as bins are sometimes moved during collection and left at the wrong address.
Timeline: Repair / Action: replacement delivered within ~21 days

service_request_type: Residential: Recycle Bin: Exchange To Medium
Description: Request a swap of your current recycling bin for a medium-sized bin that better matches your household's recycling volume.
Tip: You can only change bin size once per year. Ensure a medium bin suits your recycling habits.

service_request_type: Residential: Recycle Bin: Exchange To Large
Description: Request a swap of your current recycling bin for a larger size to accommodate higher recycling volume.
Tip: You can only change bin size once per year. Ensure the larger size is right for your needs.

service_request_type: Residential: Recycle Bin: Exchange To Extra Large
Description: Request a swap of your current blue recycling bin for an extra-large bin to accommodate higher recycling volume.
Tip: You can only change bin size once per year. Ensure the extra-large size is appropriate for your needs.

service_request_type: Residential: Recycle Bin: Additional Extra Large
Description: Request an additional extra-large blue recycling bin for your household if your current recycling volume exceeds one bin.
Tip: Additional bins may be subject to a fee. Check your current waste tier before requesting.

Description: Report that your City-issued garbage bin has gone missing or been stolen from your property.
Tip: Check nearby properties first. Bins are sometimes moved during collection and left at the wrong address.
Timeline: Repair / Action: replacement delivered within ~21 days

service_request_type: Residential: Garbage Bin: Exchange To Small
Description: Request a swap of your current garbage bin for a smaller-sized bin that better suits your household's waste output.
Tip: A smaller bin means lower waste fees. Confirm the size is sufficient before requesting the change.

service_request_type: Residential: Garbage Bin: Exchange To Medium
Description: Request a swap of your current garbage bin for a medium-sized bin that better fits your household's waste volume.
Tip: You can only change bin size once per year. Make sure the medium size is right before requesting.

service_request_type: Residential: Garbage Bin: Exchange To Large
Description: Request a swap of your current garbage bin for a larger-sized bin that better fits your household's waste volume.
Tip: A larger bin means higher waste fees. Confirm you need the upgrade before requesting the change.

service_request_type: Residential: Garbage Bin: Exchange To Extra Large
Description: Request a swap of your current garbage bin for an extra-large bin to accommodate a larger household waste volume.
Tip: Extra-large bins come with higher waste fees. Confirm the upgrade is necessary before requesting.

service_request_type: Residential: Bin: Wrong Delivery Or Bin Return
Description: Report that a City waste bin was delivered to the wrong address, or that your bin was not returned to its proper location after collection.
Tip: Check surrounding properties as bins are sometimes misplaced by collectors and may be a few doors down.

Description: Report large furniture items left at the curb that were missed during scheduled bulky item collection. Use this the day after your scheduled pickup.
Tip: Ensure furniture is placed at the curb by 7 AM on your collection day to avoid a missed pickup.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

Description: Report a City-issued garbage bin with a broken or missing wheel that makes it difficult to move to the curb.
Tip: Note your bin serial number (on the side) when filing to speed up the service.
Timeline: Repair / Action: repaired or replaced within ~7 days

Description: Report a cracked or broken lid on your City-issued garbage bin. Use this if the lid no longer closes properly or is missing entirely.
Tip: Note your bin serial number (printed on the side) when filing to speed up the replacement.

service_request_type: Residential Bin Body Or Handle Damaged
Description: Report a cracked, broken, or structurally damaged garbage bin body or handle that makes the bin unusable or unsafe to move.
Tip: Do not place the damaged bin out for collection until it has been replaced as it may not be emptied.

service_request_type: Residential / Yard Waste / Not Picked Up
Description: Report that your yard waste (leaves, grass clippings, branches) was not collected on your scheduled pickup day.
Tip: Yard waste must be in paper bags or City-approved containers; loose piles may be skipped by collectors.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Res / Yard Waste Multiple Addresses / Not Picked Up
Description: Report a missed yard waste collection affecting multiple residential addresses on the same street or route.
Tip: List all affected addresses in your report to avoid each household filing separately.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

Description: Report that your blue recycling bin was not collected on your scheduled pickup day.
Tip: Ensure recyclables are sorted correctly as contaminated bins may be intentionally left behind.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Res / Recycle / Multiple Addresses / Not Picked Up
Description: Report a missed recycling collection affecting multiple addresses on the same street or collection route.
Tip: List all affected addresses in one report rather than filing separately for each.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Res / Organic Green Bin / Not Picked Up
Description: Report that your green organics bin was not emptied on your scheduled collection day.
Tip: Line your bin with a compostable bag to reduce odour and make cleanup easier between pickups.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Res / Organic Green Bin / Multiple Addresses / Not Picked Up
Description: Report a missed green organics collection affecting multiple residential addresses on the same street or route.
Tip: Filing a single report for multiple addresses is more efficient;  list all affected addresses in the notes.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

Description: Report that your residential garbage was not collected on your scheduled pickup day. Use this if your bin was at the curb on time and the truck passed without collecting it.
Tip: Place your bin at the curb by 7 AM. Reports filed Monday or over the weekend will enter the queue and will be resolved from the following Tuesday
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Res / Garbage / Multiple Addresses Not Picked Up
Description: Report a missed garbage collection affecting multiple addresses on the same street or collection route.
Tip: A single report covering multiple addresses is processed more efficiently than individual submissions.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

Description: Request Toronto Water to restore the water supply to your property after it has been shut off.
Tip: Ensure all indoor taps are closed before the water is turned back on to prevent accidental flooding.
Timeline: Repair / Action: service restored within ~8 hours

Description: Request Toronto Water to shut off the water supply to your property, typically for plumbing repairs or renovations.
Tip: Coordinate with your plumber before filing so work can begin immediately after the shutoff.
Timeline: Repair / Action: service completed within ~8 hours

service_request_type: Report An Encroachment On City Property
Description: Report a structure, fence, landscaping, or other private installation that appears to extend onto City-owned land or the road allowance.
Tip: Include photos if possible, along with the civic address and a description of what is encroaching.

Description: Request a replacement for a lost or stolen green organic bin at your residential property.
Tip: Use a compostable bag in a temporary container until your new bin arrives.

Description: Register your property with Toronto Water for new water service, or update your account information for billing and service purposes.
Tip: Have your property address and ownership documents ready when completing the registration.

Description: Request printed materials from Solid Waste Management, such as collection calendars, recycling guides, or waste diversion information.
Tip: Most materials are also available online at toronto.ca. The digital version is often more current.

Description: Report a property that appears to violate City maintenance or safety standards, such as structural disrepair, unsafe conditions, or bylaw breaches.
Tip: Include the full property address and a clear description of the issue to help officers prioritize the inspection.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~24 hours (urgent) or ~5–10 days
Repair / Action: Investigation & enforcement process

Description: Report illegal postering on City property or structures such as traffic poles, transit shelters, or other public infrastructure. Community notices (lost pets, yard sales, cultural or religious events) are permitted on utility poles only — all other postering must be on designated City kiosks or message boards.
Tip: Include a photo and the exact location (street address or nearest intersection) of the illegal posting to help enforcement officers locate and remove it quickly.
Timeline:
Initial Response: 24 hours to 10 days depending on priority
Repair / Action: removal scheduled

Description: Request collection of a dead wild animal (raccoon, fox, bird, etc.) from a public road, sidewalk, or City property.
Tip: Do not touch or move the animal and report the exact location including nearest cross street.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~5 days
Restoration / Completion: up to ~2 weeks

Description: Request collection of a deceased dog, cat, or other domestic animal from a City street or public property.
Tip: Do not move the animal. Provide the exact address or nearest intersection when filing.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~5 days
Restoration / Completion: up to ~2 weeks

Description: Report a concern or violation related to the use of a City park, such as prohibited activities, after-hours use, or misuse of park facilities.
Tip: Parks Enforcement officers patrol regularly. Filing a report helps them prioritize specific areas.

service_request_type: Outcome Of Service Complaint Road Operations
Description: File a follow-up complaint if you are unsatisfied with the outcome or resolution of a previous Road Operations service request.
Tip: Include your original service request number to help staff locate your case quickly.

service_request_type: Multi Res / Garbage Front End / Not Picked Up
Description: Report a missed garbage collection for a front-end (dumpster) service at a multi-residential building.
Tip: Notify your property manager. They may need to coordinate access or scheduling with the contractor.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Multi Res / Furniture Pile / Not Picked Up
Description: Report bulky furniture left at the curb for collection at a multi-residential property that was not picked up as scheduled.
Tip: Coordinate with your property manager to ensure furniture is placed at the right location for collection.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

service_request_type: Missing / Damaged Street Or Traffic Signs
Description: Report a street name sign, stop sign, or other traffic sign that is missing, vandalized, or damaged and needs replacement.
Tip: Note the exact intersection and which sign is affected to help crews locate and replace it efficiently.

Description: Report a maintenance hole (manhole) cover that is loose, missing, damaged, blocked, or creating a flooding or safety hazard for pedestrians, cyclists, or vehicles.
Tip: If the cover is completely missing or poses an immediate danger, call 311 directly rather than filing online — it can be flagged as an emergency hazard for same-day response.
Timeline:
Initial Response: within ~24–72 hours depending on hazard
Repair / Action: scheduled repair
Restoration / Completion: may extend for structural work

service_request_type: Long Grass And Prohibited Plants On Private Property
Description: Report a private property with grass or weeds exceeding the City's 20 cm height limit, or prohibited invasive plants.
Tip: Include the full address and a brief description of the vegetation to help officers assess the complaint.

service_request_type: Litter / Bin / Overflow Or Not Picked Up
Description: Report an overflowing public litter bin that has not been emptied, or a litter collection that was missed during scheduled service.
Tip: Overflowing bins near parks or transit stops can be flagged as urgent when filing.
Timeline: Repair / Action: resolved within ~24 hours (if request created between Tues-Fri)

Description: Request an investigation into a missing, damaged, incorrectly placed, or ineffective regulatory sign — including stop signs, yield signs, turn prohibitions, speed limits, no parking/stopping signs, accessible parking zones, lane designations, pedestrian crossover signs, and community safety zone markers.
Tip: Note the exact intersection, the direction the sign faces, and the type of sign when filing — this significantly speeds up the investigation

Description: Report an animal welfare concern such as a pet left without adequate shelter, on a short tether, in unsanitary conditions, or where the owner has too many animals. Also covers urgent situations where a pet owner has been hospitalized, incarcerated, or evicted and their animal requires immediate protective care.
Tip: Provide as much detail as possible including the owner's address, type of animal, and nature of the concern — without an owner address, officers may not be able to act

Description: Report a wild animal that appears injured, sick, or trapped and requires assistance from Toronto Animal Services.
Tip: Keep people and pets away from the animal. Do not attempt to handle it yourself.

Description: Report an injured dog, cat, or other domestic animal in a public area that requires urgent care from Animal Services.
Tip: Keep people and other animals away from the injured animal until the officer arrives.

service_request_type: Illegal Snow Dumping & Failure To Clear Snow Or Ice On Public Sidewalk
Description: Report snow being illegally dumped onto a City sidewalk, or a property owner who has failed to clear the adjacent sidewalk as required by bylaw.
Tip: Property owners must clear adjacent sidewalks within 12 hours after a snowfall ends. This is a bylaw obligation.

Description: Report a vehicle or structure in violation of off-street parking regulations on City property — including front yard parking, boulevard parking, or use of a City street allowance without a valid permit
Tip: If reporting a vehicle on private property (common in Scarborough, North York, and Etobicoke), check whether a permit is in place before filing — licensed locations are listed on the City's website.

Description: Report an icy City-maintained sidewalk that requires salting or sanding to make it safe for pedestrians.
Tip: Wear appropriate footwear and take alternate routes until the sidewalk has been treated.

Description: Schedule collection of household hazardous waste such as paint, chemicals, batteries, or electronics that cannot go in regular garbage.
Tip: Package hazardous materials in sealed, labeled containers before your pickup date.
Timeline: Repair / Action: collected within ~24 hours of scheduled date

Description: Report graffiti on City-owned property, infrastructure, or public spaces that needs to be removed.
Tip: Photograph the graffiti and note the location clearly as this helps crews prioritize and locate it efficiently.

Description: Request general maintenance for a City-owned street tree, including inspection, cable bracing, or minor structural work.
Tip: Requests filed in summer take longer as crews focus on emergencies during the peak growing season.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~8 weeks
Repair / Action: up to ~6 months

Description: Request pruning of a City-owned street tree to remove dead branches, improve clearance, or maintain healthy growth.
Tip: Timeframes Longer if request filed between June and September
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~8 weeks
Repair / Action: up to ~6 months

Description: Request removal of a snow windrow blocking your residential driveway that was created by City snow plowing operations.
Tip: Main roads and transit routes are plowed first. Local residential streets may take longer.Multiple rounds might be needed (values provided for one round).
Timeline: Repair / Action: cleared within ~14 hours (once snowfall stops)

Description: Request an investigation into a privately owned tree that appears dead, diseased, or structurally unsound and may pose a risk to people or property.
Tip: The City can order property owners to remove dangerous trees. Inspectors will assess the risk level.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~72 hours
Restoration / Completion: up to ~12 months

Description: Report a cracked, heaved, or broken concrete sidewalk panel that is a tripping hazard or makes the sidewalk unusable.
Tip: Temporary hazard marking may be placed while the repair is queued. The full fix can take time due to volume.
Timeline:
Initial Response: ~5 business days
Restoration / Completion: may extend up to years

service_request_type: Curb Day Collection Staff Complaint Solid Waste Management
Description: File a complaint about the behaviour or conduct of a Solid Waste Management staff member during a curbside collection visit.
Tip: Provide the date, time, and location of the incident along with a clear description when filing.

service_request_type: Curb Day Collection Complaint Solid Waste Management
Description: File a complaint about the quality, conduct, or outcome of a curbside collection service such as bins not returned properly, missed stops, or unprofessional behaviour.
Tip: Note the date of collection, your address, and a description of the issue when filing.

Description: File a complaint about a City-hired contractor doing road or infrastructure work â€” for example, poor workmanship, improper site conditions, or failure to follow standards.
Tip: Note the permit number or work order if visible on posted site signage to speed up the investigation.
Timeline: Repair / Action: reviewed within ~5 business days

Description: Report excessive or after-hours noise from a nearby construction site that violates the City's noise bylaws.
Tip: Construction is permitted Mon-Fri 7 AM-7 PM and Sat 9 AM-7 PM; work outside these hours may be in violation.

Description: Request the City to pick up improperly discarded needles, syringes, or other sharps found on City property — including roads, sidewalks, boulevards, laneways, and City parks. Do not touch or attempt to remove sharps yourself.
Tip: Note the exact location (address and nearest intersection) when filing and indicate whether it is on a sidewalk, boulevard, laneway, or in a park.

service_request_type: Clean Up Litter On Sidewalks And Boulevards
Description: Request cleanup of litter, and human waste accumulated on City sidewalks or boulevards that has not been addressed through regular maintenance.
Tip: For large amounts of litter in a park or public space, use the appropriate parks or waste enforcement request instead.

Description: Request cleanup of accumulated litter in a City laneway that has not been addressed through regular operations.
Tip: Include the laneway name or bounding streets to help crews identify the correct location.

service_request_type: Clean Up Illegal Dumping On City Road Allowance
Description: Report illegally dumped garbage or materials in the City road allowance, the public strip of land between private property and the road.
Tip: Provide the nearest civic address or intersection to help crews locate the dumping quickly.

Description: Report debris such as wood, glass, furniture, or fallen materials on a City road that poses a hazard to drivers or cyclists.
Tip: For immediate traffic hazards, also call 311 directly so the issue can be flagged as urgent.

Description: Report a catch basin (storm drain) that is blocked by debris and causing water to pool on the road or sidewalk.
Tip: Do not attempt to clear the catch basin yourself. Report the location and note any flooding extent.

Description: Report a boulevard, City right-of-way, or hydro corridor section where grass or weeds have grown excessively and require cutting. The City contracts vendors to perform up to 7 scheduled grass cuts per year between May and November, with cuts spaced roughly 3 weeks apart.
Tip: If the overgrowth is creating a visibility or safety hazard (e.g. blocking a sightline at an intersection), note that when filing — it may be flagged for priority attention outside the regular schedule.

Description: Report damaged or deteriorated asphalt on a City boulevard (the paved area between the road and sidewalk).
Tip: Note the street address and which direction the damage is on (north, south, etc.) for faster dispatch.

Description: Report damage to a City boulevard caused by a snow plow, such as damaged grass, landscaping, or sod.
Tip: Boulevard restoration after winter damage is typically addressed in the spring season.

Description: File a general complaint about City-issued waste bins such as a bin being placed at the wrong property, bin quality issues, or service concerns not covered by other categories.
Tip: Include your civic address, bin type, and a clear description of the issue to help staff investigate.

Description: Request an investigation into a service issue related to your City-issued waste bins, such as an incorrect bin being assigned to your property or a billing dispute.
Tip: Have your civic address and bin serial number ready to help staff locate your account.

Description: Report persistent or excessive noise from an animal, such as a dog barking continuously, that is causing a disturbance.
Tip: Try to provide the owner's address. Without that information, bylaw officers cannot take action.

Description: Report excessive noise from amplified music or musical instruments coming from a residence, venue, or outdoor space.
Tip: Note the time, date, address, and type of noise to help bylaw officers verify the complaint.

Description: Report a landlord or property owner who is failing to maintain adequate indoor heat in a rental unit as required by City standards.
Tip: Landlords must maintain a minimum indoor temperature of 21°C during the heating season.

Description: Request an extra green organic bin for your household if your current bin is not sufficient for your food waste volume.
Tip: Additional bins may incur a fee depending on your current waste service tier.
